newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES HOLD STABLE IN LIQUID MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES HOLD STABLE IN LIQUID MARKET.

text.p: Short-term interest rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted largely stable at their overnight levels in quiet trade on Wednesday, with dealers expecting no major changes in the next two days.
"It's fairly quiet but the market is very liquid and there is little sign we will see any new developments or rate changes this week," one dealer said.
Liquidity was high on maturities of weekly treasury bills, he said but surplus estimates were not immediately available.
Discount houses were buying NCD bills redeemable after 30, 60 and 90 days at around 28 percent across the board and selling them at 22 percent.

Call money was quoted at 20 percent, down from Tuesday's 22 percent, but bankers' acceptance bills (BAs) were being bought and sold at 22 and 21 percent respectively -- unchanged from the previous day.
